caption_lesson:
🌙 Night shift, PACU (post-anesthesia care unit), 12:35 AM. He's 66, just out of an emergency hernia repair.
• Anesthesia: a gas (sevoflurane) and succinylcholine
• Jaw tight, heart rate 132, exhaled CO2 (carbon dioxide) climbing. Temp 37.9 °C

❌ 3 mistakes
1️⃣ "No fever, can't be it." Waited
2️⃣ Treated it like a post-op fever: a fever pill and ice packs, nothing more
3️⃣ Never called for help or the malignant hyperthermia cart
➡️ 41.3 °C, irregular heartbeat, dark urine, BP (blood pressure) 80/46. Rapid response.

🔥 Malignant hyperthermia (FEVER IS LATE)
• An inherited muscle reaction to inhaled anesthesia gases (like sevoflurane, not nitrous oxide) and succinylcholine
• Muscles burn energy out of control: heat, CO2, acid, potassium
• EARLY: rising exhaled CO2, fast heart rate, rigid jaw and muscles, fast breathing
• LATE: high fever, dark cola-colored urine (muscle breakdown), irregular heartbeat

✅ The right move
• Call for help and the malignant hyperthermia cart now
• Dantrolene IV (intravenous), as ordered, fast. It's the antidote
• Stop the trigger drugs. Cool the patient with ice packs and cold IV saline, as ordered, alongside dantrolene, never instead of it
• Watch potassium, the heart rhythm and urine output
• Fever pills don't fix it

🧠 Malignant hyperthermia: fever is late. Dantrolene first.

rn_checks: Triggers: volatile anesthetic gases (sevoflurane, desflurane, isoflurane) and succinylcholine; nitrous oxide is safe (MHAUS)
Early signs: unexplained rising end-tidal CO2, tachycardia, masseter and generalized rigidity, tachypnea; hyperthermia is often a late sign (MHAUS)
Late: high fever, myoglobinuria (dark urine), hyperkalemia, arrhythmias
Treatment: call for help and the MH cart, stop triggers, dantrolene IV (2.5 mg/kg, repeat as needed) as ordered, active cooling, treat potassium and arrhythmias, monitor urine
Cooling (ice packs, cold IV saline) is correct MHAUS therapy above 39 °C; the mistake shown is cooling and a fever pill ALONE, with no call and no dantrolene
Setting: onset in the PACU within the first hour after anesthesia. Realistic? End-tidal CO2 shown on PACU monitoring: OK?
Story numbers: heart rate 132, EtCO2 62, temps 37.9, 39.4, 41.3 °C, BP 80/46 over about 45 minutes. Realistic?
